title: Console IA: Surface Compass + Workspace Chip Strip (prototype & review)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: The current console sidebar and workspace switcher are dense and make it hard for engineers to rapidly jump between workspaces, see active rollouts, or get cost context for routes. Goal: Deliver a lightweight Surface Compass — a compact, contextual navigation strip at the top of the console that surfaces workspace chips, active rollout badges, and a cost-lens toggle. Provide a prototype for engineering and PM review and validate with quick usability sessions. Scope includes IA updates, wireframes, high-fidelity prototype in Figma, and annotated handoff for front-end implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates top-level Surface Compass with 3 usage states: collapsed, semi-expanded (chips), and expanded (quick actions + cost snapshot)
Workspace chip interactions: click-to-switch, long-press/hotkey to open workspace menu, hover to reveal role-specific badges
Rollout badges show canary/active percentage and click opens rollout panel
Cost-lens toggle available on the compass and reflects per-route cost deltas from the last 24h
Figma file with components, tokens, and interaction specs shared; dev-ready annotations and a small token map provided
Usability sessions with at least 6 internal users recorded and top 5 issues triaged and documented
design_notes: Rational: Move frequently used workspace controls into a single horizontal strip to reduce visual scanning and preserve left rail for persistent tools (logs, infra, settings)
Chip affordance: 40px height, 8px rounded, icon + 1-line label, compact avatar for owner; overflow uses an inline +n menu rather than an overflow drawer to preserve vertical space
Rollout badge: small circular pill that shows color + percentage; color semantic maps to rollout health (green/yellow/red) per backend signal
Cost snapshot: micro-chart sparkline with delta compared to 24h baseline and tooltip showing token breakdown (generation vs embedding)
decisions: Keep left rail persistent for global tools; Surface Compass is complementary and focused on workspace/context switching and immediate status (rollouts/cost)
Prefer inline overflow (+n) pattern over full dropdown to reduce clicks for users who switch between the top 3 workspaces frequently
Expose cost-lens as a lightweight toggle (opt-in) rather than default to avoid noise for new users
